## Overview

This Adyen POS loyalty overview describes recognizing shoppers from data returned in card-acquisition and payment responses, without requiring a physical loyalty card. A merchant can use that recognition to offer tailored benefits or recommendations and can enroll an unrecognized shopper at a payment terminal. The merchant creates and maintains customer profiles in its own backend. This dated overview does not define a complete identity, consent, security, account-permission, payment, or loyalty-program lifecycle. [[adyen]] [[adyen-pos-loyalty]]

## Key takeaways

- Recognition is based on data received in card-acquisition and payment responses. If a shopper is recognized, the page suggests on-the-spot discounts or recommendations based on purchase history; if not, it says the shopper can be enrolled at the terminal. These are possible merchant loyalty actions, not automatic terminal behavior or a guaranteed identification match. See **Shopper loyalty**, pinned raw lines 15–21.
- The merchant needs backend customer profiles containing whichever response data it uses for recognition and other use-case data, such as purchase history. The overview does not say Adyen hosts or synchronizes a unified customer profile across channels. See pinned raw line 23.
- The page routes to two distinct child topics. **Card and shopper identifiers** mentions shopper reference and email supplied with requests plus the payment card's **card alias**. **NFC wallet pass data** concerns loyalty account data linked to a merchant-created digital pass the shopper can add to an NFC wallet. The page does not equate a wallet pass with a payment token, raw PAN, or online-checkout identity. See **Next steps**, pinned raw lines 25–35.
- This hub does not describe consent collection, privacy or retention rules, card-data handling, SCA, account permissions, enrollment fields, identifier stability, response-field availability, discount application, or payment authorization. Those controls and behaviors require the relevant child guides and merchant-specific review before implementation. See complete pinned raw lines 15–35.

quotes.text: With Adyen, you can set up a loyalty program where shoppers do not need to have a physical loyalty card. Instead, you identify shoppers based on data that you receive in card acquisition and payment responses.

If you recognize a shopper from identifiers in API responses, you can offer tailored benefits like discounts on the spot, or make product recommendations based on their purchase history. If you do not recognize a shopper, you can enroll them on the spot using the payment terminal.

To use this method, you need to create customer profiles in your back-end system. A customer profile should contain the response data that you use to identify the shopper, together with any other details that your use case requires, such as purchase history data.
[The shopper reference and shopper email that you provide with your requests, and the card alias of the credit or debit card that the shopper uses.](/point-of-sale/loyalty/payment-data)
[Loyalty account data that are linked to a digital pass that you set up and that the shopper can add to their NFC wallet.](/point-of-sale/loyalty/wallet-passes)

## Definition

Adyen's 2026-09-15 POS loyalty overview describes a merchant loyalty pattern in which card-acquisition or payment-response identifiers can be used to recognize a shopper without a physical loyalty card. A merchant may offer a recognized shopper a discount or purchase-history recommendation, or enroll an unrecognized shopper at a payment terminal. The merchant must create and maintain backend customer profiles containing the response data it uses for recognition and any other needed details. [[source-adyen-docs-point-of-sale-loyalty]]

## Evidence boundary

The overview routes to separate guides for request-supplied shopper reference/email and card alias, and for loyalty-account data linked to an NFC wallet pass. It does not say these identifiers are interchangeable, persistent across all channels, raw PAN, network payment tokens, or proof of consent. It does not specify privacy retention, SCA, account permissions, enrollment fields, matching accuracy, benefit application, or a completed payment. Keep POS recognition distinct from online checkout identity or a unified customer profile until those claims have direct evidence.
